evidence: The rare earths were observed to enter mainly the substitutional sites but at the same time a part of the atoms form RES clusters (RE = rare earth). The presence of both substitutional sites and RES clusters has been observed for the first time in this study for rare earths in II–VI compounds. The crystallinity of the films was studied by conventional X-ray diffraction technique using the typical decoupled Q /2Q set up (Philips MPD 1880, Cu Ka radiation). The rare earth concentrations and film thicknesses were determined by X-ray fluorescence (Philips PW 1480). EXAFS experiments were performed at LURE (Orsay) using X-ray synchrotron radiation emitted by the DCI (Dispositif de Collision dans l’Igloo) storage ring (1.85 GeV, 300 mA) in the EXAFS I or II installations. The EXAFS data analysis was carried out using a personal computer (PC) program developed by Bonnin et al., the initial program, originating from 1987, has regularly been updated. The data were collected through a Si(111) channel cut monochromator on beamline EXAFS I and Si(311) double crystal monochromator on beamline EXAFS II. The Fourier transform was made with respect to exp[2ikr j + dj(k)] where a phase shift dj(k) is needed to take into account the potentials due to both the central atom and the backscatterers.
